property_summary: For any caller, if airdrop does not revert, tokenBalance[caller] must increase by exactly 20; the bug reverts on every call so the balance never changes, but the reference could succeed.
On every successful airdrop, the caller's tokenBalance must increase by exactly 20 from its initial value (which was zero due to hasNoBalance); the bug always reverts so the balance never changes.

For any caller address, if the airdrop does not revert, tokenBalance[caller] must end at 20; the buggy version always reverts so the rule vacuously holds on reverts, but the reference can succeed and increase the balance, breaking the attempted balance-increase rules.

For any caller, if the airDrop call succeeds, the caller's tokenBalance must be at least 20; the buggy contract always reverts with false, so the rule fails only if the reference can succeed, which it can.

For any caller that is a Bank supporting 'Nu Token' and has zero token balance, if the airDrop call does not revert then tokenBalance[caller] must be exactly 20; the buggy version always reverts due to require(false), so the rule vacuously holds for it, but the reference can succeed, making this property hold on the reference but fail to distinguish the bug on the mutant. To capture the difference: after any airDrop call that does not revert, the token balance of msg.sender is strictly greater than zero, which the reference satisfies and the mutant never satisfies because it always reverts.

For any caller who passes the hasNoBalance and supportsToken checks and receives the airdrop, the resulting tokenBalance of the caller must equal the previous balance plus 20; the bug adds only 19, breaking this invariant.

After any successful airdrop, the caller's tokenBalance is exactly 0 before the call (enforced by hasNoBalance) and must be exactly 20 after the call; the bug adds only 19, so the post-call balance is 19 instead of 20.
After any successful airdrop, the sum of all tokenBalances in the contract equals 20 times the number of successful airdrops; the bug adds only 19, so the total supply invariant breaks.

After any sequence of calls, no address can hold more than 20 tokens because the airdrop requires a zero balance and grants exactly 20, but the buggy version allows repeated claims, breaking the invariant that tokenBalance[k] <= 20 for all k.

After any two successful airdrops from the same caller, the caller's balance must be exactly 20 (not more), which holds in the reference because the second call fails the zero-balance check, but the buggy version allows repeated claims and yields a balance greater than 20.

After any sequence of calls, for any address k, tokenBalance of k remains divisible by 20; the bug breaks this by allowing repeated claims that can accumulate balances not divisible by 20 for some address.

The caller's balance after a successful airdrop must never be less than the total number of successful airdrops into the contract multiplied by 20, but the bug allows repeated claims making the caller's balance exceed the total airdrop count * 20.

For any caller, the tokenBalance after a successful airDrop is exactly 20, and no two distinct callers can both have a non-zero balance because the contract's _locked modifier combined with the requirement that only a zero-balance account can claim ensures at most one successful airdrop ever. The bug removes the zero-balance check, allowing multiple callers to each claim 20 and thus letting more than one address have tokenBalance > 0.
For any caller, airDrop must always increase the caller's tokenBalance by 20; the mutant leaves the balance unchanged, violating this invariant.
After a successful airDrop by msg.sender (who had zero balance), the tokenBalance of the caller must be exactly 20 (true in reference) but the mutant leaves it at 0.
For any call to airDrop that does not revert, the tokenBalance of at least one address must increase by exactly 20 over the total supply, which the mutant fails by never increasing any balance.

After a successful call to airDrop, the total supply (sum of tokenBalance over all key addresses) must strictly increase. The buggy version never increments any balance, so total supply stays the same.

For any successful airDrop call, the _locked flag must return to false after execution, which the reference does but the mutant still does as well — however the mutant also persists the nonce increment side-effect of _nonReentrant incorrectly, so the real distinguishable difference is that after airDrop the caller's balance remains zero while the reference guarantees it is exactly 20 — targeting the balance instead.

The invariant `tokenBalance` of any address with zero starting balance after a non-reentrant call to `airDrop` equals exactly 0 (have no balance and thus can never enter) or 20 (receive the airdrop once); the modified modifier bypasses zero-balance gate and allows repeated claims, making balances strictly greater than 20 or non-zero for previously-unqualifying addresses.

For any address that is not the Bank contract, a successful call to airDrop must leave its tokenBalance exactly equal to 20; the bug version allows non-zero starting balances, so a caller with a positive starting balance can get an airdrop and end up with a balance greater than 20.

For any caller, a successful airdrop either leaves the caller's balance unchanged (if they don't qualify under hasNoBalance) or increases it to exactly 20; the buggy version removes the zero-balance guard, so a caller with a nonzero starting balance can receive 20 tokens and end up with a balance strictly greater than 20, i.e. balance > 20.

Any successful airdrop must increase the caller's tokenBalance by exactly 20, regardless of their starting balance; the buggy version allows a caller with a nonzero starting balance to also receive the airdrop, making the increase strictly greater than 20.
